As part of the creative core team for a faculty-wide event welcoming over
1,000 new students, I took full ownership of shaping the event's visual identity
across both digital and print mediums. My primary responsibility was curating
the "face of the event" aka designing the entire series of Instagram feeds,
carousels, and stories that served as the main promotional frontline. Beyond
social media, I also crafted large-format physical assets such as main stage
backdrops, banners, and signage, ensuring every touchpoint, whether onscreen or on-ground, felt cohesive, fun, and professionally branded.
What truly defined this experience for me, however, was the opportunity
to step beyond my designated scope. During the preparation phase, I was
entrusted with a larger responsibility: to oversee one of the main segments,
Dekan Cup. In this capacity, I acted as the primary communication bridge
with the Event division, personally coordinating the visual themes, Instagram
feed concepts, and overall creative direction to ensure every asset perfectly
captured the segment's unique identity. At one point, a miscommunication
arose between divisions regarding the visual direction and timelines, but I
quickly stepped up to realigning expectations and finding a middle ground that
satisfied all parties, without derailing our production schedule.
This role taught me that great event execution isn't just about producing
beautiful visuals, it's about being adaptable, responsive, and willing to step
up when the team needs you. Whether it was taking ownership of a major
segment's creative direction, resolving miscommunications constructively, or
learning an entirely new technical skill on the fly, I walked away with a deeper
appreciation for cross-division collaboration and the confidence to handle
uncertainty with a calm, problem-solving mindset.

Design, Documentation, and Multimedia Division - INTRIVIA 2025
May 2025 - October 2025 (6 months)
Malang

Joining the creative team for INTRIVIA 2025, a department-level event that
gathered over 200 attendees, I quickly learned that speed and precision go
hand in hand. My days were filled with executing rapid-turnaround digital and
print materials, from event posters and banners to social media assets and
documentation kits. Every request came with a tight timeline, pushing me to
work efficiently without sacrificing visual quality. I thrived on this fast-paced

rhythm, discovering that some of my best work came from those moments
when the clock was ticking the loudest.
I actively welcomed real-time feedback from the core committee, embracing
sudden changes and additional requests as opportunities to refine rather than
obstacles. However, the most unexpected challenge came just days before the
event, when I was suddenly assigned to create the main bumper and several
additional motion graphics for the main stage, a task I had absolutely zero prior
experience in. With no background in motion design and a fast-approaching
deadline, I threw myself into self-learning, binge-watching tutorials, and
experimenting with animation timelines during those crunch days. Against all
odds, I successfully delivered a polished set of bumpers right on schedule,
proving that a willingness to learn can often outrun a lack of prior skill.
Looking back, INTRIVIA 2025 gave me a front-row seat to the power of
teamwork and adaptability. I learned that great collaboration isn't about
avoiding changes, but about embracing them with a positive mindset and
a willingness to adjust, whether that means accommodating last-minute
revisions or diving headfirst into unfamiliar creative territories like motion
graphics. More than just sharpening my design skills, this experience
transformed me into a fearless learner and a dependable teammate, someone
who can create under pressure, pivot when needed, and show up both onscreen and on-site.

Design, Documentation, and Multimedia Division - TECHPRENEUR
2025
April 2025 - October 2025 (7 months)
Malang

Being part of TECHPRENEUR 2025, a national-scale business plan
competition, meant operating within a deliberately small and agile DDM team
where every deadline felt personal and every task demanded exceptional
precision. I maintained an obsessive eye for detail, meticulously cross-verifying
every piece of textual content to ensure zero errors in public-facing materials.
This rigorous verification process was essential to uphold the professionalism
expected of a national-level event watched by participants from across
Indonesia.
Working in such a compact team meant juggling all DDM responsibilities
simultaneously, from social media content and promotional graphics to print
production and documentation requests, without letting anything slip. This

required sharp time management and the ability to prioritize shifting tasks on
the fly while keeping every deliverable on schedule.
Looking back, TECHPRENEUR 2025 taught me that in a small team,
accountability isn't just a value, it's a necessity. I learned to take full ownership
of my deliverables while trusting my teammates completely, ensuring we
maintained accuracy and composure even when multitasking at full throttle.
The experience deepened my commitment to discipline and reliability, qualities
I continue to carry into every professional challenge I take on.
